## Digital Marketing Agency in Pune: What Google's Local Services Ads Expansion Means for Local Businesses in 2026

Google's Local Services Ads (LSA) program — the pay-per-lead ads with a verification badge that appear above regular Search ads for categories like plumbers, electricians, lawyers, and home-care providers — has spent the past three years expanding aggressively in the United States and a handful of other markets. For a digital marketing agency in Pune fielding questions from clients about it, the honest, unglamorous answer as of September 2026 is this: Local Services Ads are not yet available for businesses operating in India, based on Google's own published list of eligible countries. That doesn't make the expansion irrelevant to a Pune clinic, home-services company, or CA firm — it previews the direction Google is taking local paid search (pay-per-lead billing, identity and licence verification, ads ranked above everything else), and it tells you what to have ready if and when the program does reach India. This article works through what LSA actually is, how it differs from a normal Google Ads Search campaign and from your free Google Business Profile listing, what Google itself says about where the program currently runs, and what a Pune-based service business should realistically do about it right now.

## What Local Services Ads Actually Are

Local Services Ads are a distinct Google product, not a setting inside a regular Search campaign. A handful of features set them apart from every other Google ad format:

**They appear above regular Search ads and the organic Map Pack.** In the countries where LSA runs, a search like "emergency plumber near me" surfaces a small block of two or three Local Services listings — business name, star rating, hours, and a badge — sitting above the paid Search ads and above the three-pack of Map listings. That's the single biggest reason home-services and professional-services businesses in eligible markets fight to get into the program: it occupies the most visible real estate on the results page, ahead of everything a competitor's Google Ads Search campaign or SEO can buy or earn.

**Billing is pay-per-lead, not pay-per-click.** A standard Google Ads Search campaign charges you every time someone clicks your ad, whether or not that person ever calls or messages you. Local Services Ads charge only when a customer contacts you directly through the ad — a phone call, a message, or (for some categories) a booking — and Google's own support documentation describes disputing and getting credited for leads that turn out to be spam, wrong-category enquiries, or duplicates. In practice this shifts the entire cost logic of the format: you're paying for contacts, not clicks, which is a meaningfully different budgeting exercise from a normal PPC account.

**Providers carry a verification badge — now called Google Verified.** For years this badge existed in two flavours: "Google Guaranteed" for home-services categories (backed by a money-back guarantee for the customer) and "Google Screened" for professional-services categories like lawyers and financial advisors (backed by licence and background checks but no guarantee). According to Google's own Local Services Help documentation, Google retired both the Google Guarantee and Google Screened badges on 20 October 2025 and replaced them with a single unified "Google Verified" badge and blue checkmark across all eligible categories, discontinuing the money-back guarantee itself (existing customers had until 7 December 2025 to file reimbursement claims for services booked before the change). If a vendor or an old blog post is still telling you to chase "Google Guaranteed" status in 2026, that specific badge no longer exists — what businesses now qualify for is Google Verified, earned through the same underlying checks: business registration, licensing where applicable, insurance, and in many categories a background check run through a third-party screening provider Google works with.

**Qualification is a screening process, not a bid.** You can't simply outbid a competitor into the top LSA slot the way you can nudge a Search ad's rank with a higher CPC. Google's qualification page describes checks that vary by category and location — business entity verification, licence checks, insurance minimums that differ by service type, and for higher-risk categories, background checks on the business owner and sometimes on individual field workers. Ranking within the Local Services block is then influenced by review volume and rating, proximity, responsiveness to leads, and how the account performs over time — closer in spirit to how the organic Map Pack ranks businesses than to a Search ads auction.

## How LSA Differs From a Regular Google Ads Search Campaign

It's easy to conflate the two because both are Google Ads products a business pays for, but they solve different problems and, in eligible markets, usually run side by side rather than as substitutes.

A standard **Google Ads Search campaign** — the kind our [Google Ads management service](/services/google-ads) runs for clients — gives you full control over keywords, ad copy, landing pages, and bidding strategy, and you pay per click regardless of what happens after someone lands on your site. It's available essentially everywhere Google Ads operates, including India, with no vetting process beyond normal ad policy compliance. You can launch a Search campaign in Pune this afternoon.

**Local Services Ads** trade that control for placement and trust signalling: less flexibility over creative and targeting, but a badge, a position above the Search ads, and a billing model tied to contacts rather than clicks — available only in the countries and categories Google has specifically opened the program to, which, again, does not currently include India.

## How LSA Differs From Your Google Business Profile and the Map Pack

The other frequent confusion is between Local Services Ads and simply having a well-optimised free Google Business Profile (GBP) listing that shows up in the organic three-pack of local results. They are not the same thing, and a business doesn't need one to have the other.

Your GBP listing and its place in the Map Pack are **free and earned**, not bought — ranking depends on relevance, distance, and prominence signals like reviews, citations, and on-page local SEO, which we cover in detail in [our guide to ranking in the Google Map Pack in 2026](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026). Local Services Ads, by contrast, are a **paid, screened product** that sits above both the Map Pack and the Search ads, in the countries where it exists. A business can run a Local Services Ad and still show up (or fail to show up) in the free Map Pack independently — the two systems use different ranking inputs, though a strong GBP profile with genuine reviews tends to help performance in both.

For a Pune business today, the practical takeaway is that Map Pack visibility and Google Ads Search campaigns are the two channels you can actually act on right now; Local Services Ads is a channel to watch, not one you can currently switch on.

## The Honest Rollout Status: Where LSA Actually Is (and Isn't) in 2026

This is the part worth getting precisely right rather than repeating what circulates on marketing blogs. Google's own "Getting started with Local Services Ads" support page presents a country selector for the program, and as of this writing that selector lists exactly eleven countries: the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and eight countries in continental Europe — Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Spain, and Switzerland. India is not among them, and we could not find an official Google page, support document, or company blog post announcing an India launch, a waitlist, or even a stated timeline for one. Google's own 2023 expansion announcement, which took the program past 70 eligible business types, likewise makes no mention of new countries — it describes broadening categories inside markets the program already served.

That's a materially different picture from "India's rollout is behind the US but underway," which is the framing you'll see on a number of Indian digital marketing blogs and agency sites. We'd treat those claims with real scepticism until you can verify them yourself on Google's official eligibility tool, because as far as the documentation we could locate shows, there currently isn't a rollout in India to be behind on — the program simply hasn't launched there. If your own attempt to sign up shows something different by the time you read this, that would be a genuine, recent change worth acting on quickly; check directly rather than taking a third party's word for it, since eligibility can change without a public announcement and this is exactly the kind of detail that goes stale fast.

**What is confirmed, and matters even if you're outside the program today, is that Google announced in 2026 that it is migrating Local Services Ads into the main Google Ads platform.** According to Google's own support documentation on the transition, the migration began in August 2026 with a limited group of U.S. home-and-storefront-service advertisers — plumbing, HVAC, electrical, appliance repair, house cleaning, lawn care, roofing, pest control, and moving — moving into a new Performance Max campaign type built specifically around pay-per-lead goals, with the standalone Local Services Ads dashboard being phased out for migrated accounts. Google's documented plan expands this to broader U.S. advertiser groups in late 2026, including service-area businesses without a physical storefront and accounts using custom bidding or booking setups, and states that non-U.S. accounts and any remaining business categories are expected to transition in 2027. We've written separately about [what the 2026 Performance Max reporting changes already mean for campaigns Pune businesses are running today](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-performance-max-2026), and the relevant overlap here is that even if and when Local Services Ads does arrive in India, the version that shows up may well already be a Performance Max pay-per-lead campaign type rather than the separate, standalone LSA dashboard that U.S. advertisers used for most of the program's history — because by the time a new market is onboarded, that may be the only version left running.

## Why Some Agencies Already Claim to "Run" Local Services Ads for Indian Clients

If you search for this topic, you'll come across Indian marketing agencies advertising Local Services Ads setup, "Google Guaranteed" certification help, or LSA management specifically for Indian businesses. We can't verify what those agencies are actually delivering, and given what Google's own country selector shows, we'd ask a direct, specific question before paying anyone for this: which Google account, in which country's eligibility flow, is this ad actually running through? A legitimate answer names a real, working campaign you can log into and see. A vague answer, or one that reroutes you toward a different product entirely (a Search campaign relabelled as "local ads," or a Google Business Profile optimisation package), is worth walking away from. This is precisely the kind of claim worth verifying against Google's own documentation rather than a vendor's landing page — the qualification and eligibility pages linked at the end of this article are free to check yourself in under ten minutes.

## What a Pune Service Business Should Actually Do Right Now

Given the honest state of the program, here's a realistic sequence for a clinic, home-services company, legal or CA firm, or similar local service business based in Pune.

**Check the live eligibility tool yourself, periodically, rather than relying on this article or anyone else's.** Google's eligibility flow is the only source that reflects the current, real-time state of the program for your specific category and location, and it costs nothing to check. Bookmark it and revisit it every few months rather than assuming today's answer will still be true in a year.

**Put your budget and effort where it actually works in India today.** That means a properly optimised Google Business Profile competing for Map Pack visibility — the free channel local searchers use constantly, covered in depth in [our Map Pack ranking guide](/blog/local-seo-google-map-pack-pune-2026) — and a well-structured [Google Ads Search campaign](/services/google-ads) for the keywords where paid intent is highest. Between the two, most Pune service businesses can build a genuinely competitive local presence without LSA being part of the mix at all, because that's the reality every Pune service business has been operating in until now.

**Get your documentation in order now, so you're not starting from zero if eligibility opens up.** LSA qualification leans on business registration details, applicable licences, insurance, and — depending on category — background checks on the business and its staff. A clinic, legal practice, or CA firm in India already holds most of the licensing and registration paperwork this kind of screening asks for; keeping it organised and current isn't wasted effort even without LSA, since the same documents matter for Google Business Profile verification, GST and professional-body compliance, and increasingly for corporate or institutional clients doing basic due diligence before they'll work with you.

**Build genuine review volume regardless of which paid channel you end up using.** Every version of Google's local ranking — the free Map Pack, a Search campaign's Quality Score, and Local Services Ads' own ranking factors in the markets where it runs — rewards a business with a healthy volume of recent, genuine reviews and penalises one that doesn't have them. This is one of the few pieces of local search advice that's genuinely channel-agnostic: it helps you today and it will help you if LSA eligibility opens up tomorrow.

**Treat "pay-per-lead" as a preview of where paid local search is heading, not a feature exclusive to LSA.** Google's own move to fold Local Services Ads into Performance Max as a pay-per-lead campaign type signals that lead-based billing, not just click-based billing, is becoming a permanent part of how Google sells local ads — a genuinely different pitch from the click-based Search campaigns most Pune businesses have run for years, and one worth understanding conceptually even before it's something you can technically buy. It's one more entry in a longer pattern worth watching if you're managing your own account rather than outsourcing it: Google has reshaped the mechanics of local and performance advertising more than once in the past couple of years, from [the Performance Max reporting overhaul](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-performance-max-2026) to [the reversal on killing third-party cookies that changed how retargeting budgets get allocated](/blog/digital-marketing-agency-pune-third-party-cookies-2026), and each of those changes has landed in India even when a specific new ad format like LSA hasn't.

## If Your Business Also Operates in an Eligible Country

A meaningful number of Pune-based businesses aren't purely local — export-oriented consultancies, professional-services firms with a U.S. or U.K.-facing arm, or franchise operators with a presence abroad. If that describes you and a US, Canadian, UK, or eligible European entity of your business wants to actually run Local Services Ads there, the real starting sequence is straightforward: run the eligibility check for that country and category first, since availability is decided at the specific service-and-location level rather than country-wide; complete the screening Google requires for that market (business verification, licensing, insurance, and any background checks the category calls for); set a weekly budget once approved, since LSA spend is capped weekly rather than through a standard daily budget; and build a habit of reviewing and disputing any leads that are clearly spam, wrong-category, or outside your service area promptly, since Google's own credit process exists specifically for that and unclaimed bad leads otherwise sit on your bill.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Are Google Local Services Ads available for businesses in Pune or elsewhere in India right now?

Based on Google's own published country list for the program as of this writing, no — the "Getting started with Local Services Ads" support page's country selector lists the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and eight European countries, and India is not among them. We couldn't find an official Google announcement of an India launch date, pilot, or waitlist. Eligibility can change without much public fanfare, so the only reliable way to know your current status is to run Google's own eligibility check for your category and city rather than trusting a blog post, including this one, to still be accurate months from now.

### How is a Local Services Ad different from a normal Google Ads Search campaign?

The core difference is what you pay for and where the ad appears. A Search campaign charges you per click on your ad, wherever it ranks among the paid results, and it's something any advertiser — including one in India — can launch today. A Local Services Ad, in the countries where it exists, appears above both the Search ads and the organic Map Pack, charges only for a genuine contact (a call, message, or booking) rather than a click, and requires the business to pass Google's screening and verification process before it can run at all.

### What's the difference between the old "Google Guaranteed" badge and the new "Google Verified" badge?

Google retired the separate Google Guaranteed and Google Screened badges on 20 October 2025 and replaced both with a single "Google Verified" badge across eligible Local Services Ads categories, according to Google's own Local Services Help documentation. The practical change for consumers is that the money-back guarantee tied to the old Google Guaranteed badge was discontinued at the same time (with a short window to claim reimbursement for services booked before the cutover); for businesses, the underlying qualification checks — licensing, insurance, and background checks appropriate to the category — are largely unchanged, just consolidated under one badge and one name.

### If Local Services Ads aren't available in India yet, what should I actually spend my marketing budget on?

For most Pune service businesses, the two channels that are both available and effective right now are a properly optimised Google Business Profile competing for Map Pack visibility and a well-run Google Ads Search campaign targeting your highest-intent local keywords. Neither requires waiting on Google to open a new program, both respond to genuine investment (accurate business information, real reviews, sound keyword and landing-page work), and both put you in a stronger position — more reviews, cleaner licensing documentation, better account history — if Local Services Ads does eventually reach India.

## Where This Leaves a Pune Business Today

The honest version of this story isn't as exciting as "Google's newest ad format is coming to India" — it's that the format isn't here yet, the countries where it does run are moving toward folding it into Performance Max rather than keeping it as a separate program, and the two channels that genuinely matter for a Pune service business right now are the same two that mattered last year: a well-run Google Business Profile and a properly structured Search campaign. At Govindani Infotech, our [SEO](/services/seo) and [Google Ads](/services/google-ads) work for Pune clients — clinics, home-services companies, and professional practices among them — is built around that reality rather than around chasing a feature we can't verify is buyable in India yet. We keep an eye on Google's eligibility documentation as part of that ongoing account management, and if Local Services Ads does open up for Indian advertisers, existing clients with strong GBP and Search foundations will be the ones positioned to move on it fastest. If you want a straight read on which of these channels is actually worth your next rupee, [get in touch through our contact page](/contact-us).
